# 0009. Identifiers are UUID v7, generated by the caller and passed into the constructor

Status: Accepted

Date: 2026-11-10

## Context

Write operations go through a command bus whose handlers return nothing
(ADR [0004](0004-layered-modules-and-cqrs-buses.md)). After dispatching a create command, the
processor still has to read the new resource back, so it needs the id before the handler runs.
Ids also appear in URLs and in the `X-Organization-Id` header, where sequential integers would reveal
how many businesses and records exist.

## Decision

1. Every entity id is a UUID v7 (`Symfony\Component\Uid\Uuid`, Doctrine type `uuid`).
2. The id is generated outside the entity, in the Ui layer (the HTTP processor, a console command or
   a fixture), passed in the command as a string, and given to the entity constructor. Entities do
   not generate their own ids, and the database does not either.
3. Commands and queries carry ids as strings; conversion to `Uuid` happens in the handler.

## Alternatives considered

- **Auto-increment integers.** The id is known only after flush, so a handler would have to return
  it, and ids would be guessable and reveal volumes.
- **UUID v4.** Random order fragments the primary-key index; v7 is time-ordered and sorts by creation
  time.

## Consequences

- Processors know the id up front and read the View back by it without the handler returning
  anything.
- Ids are not guessable, which complements but does not replace the tenant filter
  (ADR [0001](0001-multi-tenancy-shared-database-organization-filter.md)).
- A retried create with the same id hits the primary key instead of creating a duplicate.
